method: Real documents, not PubChem grids: the pixel-exact method of build_ground_truth.py does not apply. All eleven files carry a text layer (measured with pdftotext: 2,400-4,500 characters per page in every file, an embedded OCR layer over the USPTO scans and real text in the three born-digital files), but the text layer was used only to FIND things - every structure was located and read by rendering the page with pdftoppm at 100 dpi and then cropping the drawing at 250-400 dpi and looking at it. Each resolved molecule required TWO independent views to agree: (a) where the document prints a full IUPAC name, OPSIN (py2opsin 1.2.0) converted the printed name to SMILES - never a PubChem name search, which on this corpus silently returned the wrong enantiomer - and where it prints only a code, trivial name or nothing, the structure was read off the drawing by hand; and (b) the RDKit InChIKey of that SMILES was looked up with PUG-REST /compound/inchikey/ (structure-keyed) and the record's drawing compared with the document's. At build time every SMILES is re-parsed with RDKit, its canonical form, connectivity SMILES, formula and InChIKey are RECOMPUTED (never copied from a database record), and the record for each CID is fetched from PubChem BY CID and its InChIKey and formula must equal the recomputed ones or the build aborts. Every stereocentre was checked with RDKit's CIP assignment against the descriptor printed in the document; where the descriptor is carried only by a wedge, the drawn geometry (neighbour directions and wedge type) was transcribed into a molblock and RDKit's interpretation of that wedge compared with the printed or expected label. Printed empirical formulae, molecular weights, HRMS values and elemental analyses were compared with RDKit values wherever they exist. Per-molecule `confidence` is one of name_match (a name, code or CAS printed in the document resolves to the CID and the drawing agrees) or drawing_read (no usable printed name; the structure was read off the drawing and confirmed by structure-keyed PubChem lookup, sometimes with a printed mass or analysis as a third view). `basis` states how each was pinned, including CID and page. Drawings without any wedge, hash or printed descriptor are referenced to the stereo-unspecified record, as in earlier rounds: a tool that invents a wedge the document does not draw is the one that is wrong. None of the eleven files is a page extract, so `page` numbers are both file pages and publication pages. `pixel_verified` is false everywhere - it is not achievable on real documents. Eight of the eleven documents were first catalogued by an independent reader following this same written method and then re-verified row by row (RDKit recompute, PubChem by CID, and a second look at the drawing) before entry; three were catalogued directly.
excluded: Structures that are DRAWN but carry no resolvable SMILES are held in each group's `unscoreable` array, NOT in `molecules`. That split is load-bearing: score_run.py calls Chem.MolFromSmiles(m['smiles']) on every entry of `molecules` and a null raises TypeError before its own error message. `unscoreable` holds Markush/R-group generics (generic: true), bracketed non-isolated species and chelates drawn with dashed coordination bonds, species whose exact InChIKey has NO PubChem record (each 404 was re-fetched directly, never taken from a cache), species whose name and drawing DISAGREE (this round has one that the issuing office itself later corrected), compounds that are named but never drawn - including, in two groups, the title drug itself - and bookkeeping rows that describe a whole class of depiction so that the arithmetic between `structures_drawn` and the row counts is legible. Repeat drawings of one compound are collapsed to ONE row, because score_run.py matches predictions to molecules by NAME and counts recall per row; enantiomer pairs drawn as pixel-identical flat structures distinguished only by a printed (+)/(-) are likewise one row on the stereo-unspecified record. One group (the GROMACS MetaDump paper) is a deliberate negative with zero depictions and empty arrays; another (the tofacitinib patent) draws 27 structures of which every one is generic, so its `molecules` array is empty although it is a positive document.

US4117118A_cyclosporin.drawing_style: Bilevel raster scan of the 1978 USPTO print with an embedded OCR text layer (41626 characters, useless for chemistry: the printed formula C62H111N11O12 comes out as 'CQHHINHOH' and the drawings as noise). All four structures are the same hand-set typographic CONDENSED formula of a cyclic undecapeptide: atom groups set as text (CH3, CH2, CH, CO, N, H, HO, C) joined by straight bond lines, side chains hung above and below two backbone rows, 85 heavy atoms filling half a page - the largest single depiction in the corpus. No wedge or hash anywhere: stereochemistry is expressed ONLY by printed capital letters beside the stereocentres (L or D at each alpha carbon, R at the two side-chain centres of the MeBmt residue), and the alkene geometry by explicit placement of its H, CH3 and CH2 substituents (trans). Three dotted lines mark intramolecular N-H...O=C hydrogen bonds and are not bonds. The 'R' letters are a trap: an OCSR tool has every reason to read them as R-groups. No IUPAC name is printed anywhere; the compounds are identified only by the codes S 7481/F-1 and S 7481/F-2 and the trivial names cyclosporin A and B.
US4117118A_cyclosporin.note: Whole 17-page document. pp2-7 are FIG. 1-6, the UV, IR and 90 MHz 1H NMR spectra of F-1 and F-2 - six built-in negatives; p8 draws S 7481/F-1, p9 draws S 7481/F-2, p14 draws both again inside claims 2 and 5; p12 carries a 13C NMR table; p16 is a Certificate of Correction. THE FINDING OF THIS GROUP: the F-2 drawings are printed atom-for-atom identical to the F-1 drawings - residue 2, between MeBmt and sarcosine, carries CH3 over CH2 over CH, an ethyl, i.e. alpha-aminobutyric acid, which is cyclosporin A's residue; cyclosporin B has alanine there - and the issuing office knew: the p16 Certificate of Correction orders 'change CH3-CH2- to CH3- in the upper right-hand portion of the formula shown for S 7481/F-2' at both locations. The scan carries the uncorrected ink. So the F-2 depiction is a name/formula/drawing disagreement documented by the document itself and is held in unscoreable, while every printed formula and HRMS for F-1 (C62H111N11O12; m/e 1183.831 for the M-H2O ion) agrees with the drawing and with PubChem's cyclosporin A. An earlier reading in the corpus notes claimed the document prints C61H109N11O12 for F-1; that is wrong - every F-1 instance (p8, p11 twice, p13) prints C62 at 300 dpi, and C61 is printed only for F-2. The confusion came from the garbled OCR layer.

Structures are black ChemDraw-style line drawings with explicit heteroatom labels and condensed groups (O2N, CO2Et, CHO, CN, EtO, MeSn, (EtO)2P(O), Ph, Hal, PG, G1/G2), no colour, and NO wedge or hash anywhere; the only stereodescriptor in the document is the '(S)' in the name of Example 12. Reaction schemes draw the reagent as a small structure above the arrow with conditions below. The front page says 'No Drawings'.
US6936612B2_palbociclib.note: Whole 41-page document, and mostly negatives: depictions occur on p1 (formula II in the abstract), p2 (formula I), p6 (formula II again) and pp13-17 (Schemes 1-13, 70 drawings); pp3-5, 7-12 and 18-41 - thirty-one pages - carry no structure at all, only text: several hundred named preferred compounds on pp6-12, Examples 1-136 on pp18-41 and the IC50 Table 1 and claims on p41. Of the 73 depictions only THIRTEEN are specific compounds, all on p13 in Schemes 2 and 3, and they are illustrative fragment syntheses (a 2-aminopyridine side chain, three 2-aminopyridine-3-carbonitrile / carboxylate ring syntheses), not the claimed compounds. Calcd for C24H29N7O2 . 2.4 H2O . 1.85 HCl'), claim 1 by name (free base), 'Compound 36b' in the formulation Examples, and row 36 of Table 1; every drawn structure carrying the piperazinyl-pyridine side chain is Markush.
